exposure: Forceps-assisted fetal head extraction during LSCS
Manual fetal head extraction during LSCS
outcome: Need for transfusion (blood, FFP, platelets, volume expanders)
U-D time (Uterine incision to delivery time)
Intraoperative events (extension/laceration-associated angle hematoma, stitch line hematoma, window at stitch site, cut through, apposition failure, major operations)
cohort: The study included 66 mothers admitted for cesarean section from ANC, antenatal OPD, and Emergency, randomized into forceps (n=33) and manual (n=33) extraction groups.
finding: Application of forceps for fetal head delivery during cesarean operation produced statistically significant better outcomes compared to manual extraction.
mod_finding: Forceps-assisted fetal head extraction during cesarean section resulted in statistically significant better maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to manual extraction.
